members.title: Turkiye keen to send experts on women’s health as Zubaida meets Emine Erdogan
members.lead: Turkiye has expressed interest in strengthening cooperation with Bangladesh in several areas, including tackling the impacts of climate change, protecting the health of women and children, renewable energy and the production of eco-friendly products. Turkiye’s First Lady Emine Erdogan has particularly expressed willingness to send a team of experts to Bangladesh to share experience and cooperate in addressing the health problems faced by women in the country’s coastal and marginalised areas due to climate change. . The matters were discussed at a meeting between Zubaida Rahman, spouse of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, and Emine Erdogan, spouse of Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and also chairperson of the Zero Waste Foundation. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam disclosed this at a press conference held on Tuesday at the Conference Room of the Papillon Ziugma Relaxury Hotel in Antalya. She said the highly fruitful meeting between Zubaida Rahman and the Turkish First Lady took place on the first day of the Bangladesh delegation’s participation in the COP31 climate summit. The two sides discussed in detail potential bilateral cooperation to tackle the impacts of climate change and its adverse effects on women and children. Shama Obaed said Emine Erdogan praised the capacity and resilience of the people of Bangladesh in facing the adversities of climate change. She also expressed interest in cooperating with Bangladesh on waste-to-energy production, solar power and other eco-friendly initiatives. . The meeting also discussed expanding the market for Bangladeshi jute products, especially eco-friendly and biodegradable ones, as an alternative to plastic, in Turkiye and other international markets. The Turkish First Lady showed particular interest in this area. members.title: Tarique Rahman-Erdogan meet takes Bangladesh-Turkiye ties to new strategic height: Humaiun
members.lead: Bangladesh-Turkiye relations have reached a new strategic height through the bilateral meeting between Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said here. The meeting, held at the Max Royal Hotel in Antalya on Tuesday evening, discussed expanding cooperation in various sectors, including trade and investment, energy, aviation and the defence industry. Both sides expressed interest in exploring the possibility of building a defence industry in Bangladesh and of joint investment in the sector, said the state minister at a press conference on Tuesday night at the Papillon Ziugma Relaxury Hotel in Antalya. . Humaiun Kobir said the meeting between the Bangladesh Prime Minister and the Turkish President took place in a warm and fraternal atmosphere. President Erdogan addressed Prime Minister Tarique Rahman as “my valuable friend and brother” and expressed interest in taking relations with Bangladesh to a higher level. Along with increasing bilateral trade and investment, partnership in the energy sector, investment in aviation and cooperation in the defence industry received importance at the meeting. Humaiun Kobir said the Bangladesh government has taken an initiative to set up a defence industrial park in the country. Prospects of Turkish investment and joint ventures in this sector were discussed. However, he said, no agreement or memorandum of understanding (MoU) has yet been signed on the matter, which remains at the stage of preliminary exploration and discussion. He said discussions on energy covered deep-sea mineral and energy exploration, renewable energy and making use of Turkiye’s experience and best practices in these areas. . Bangladesh is keen to build a strong investment partnership with Turkiye in these sectors.
